subject.title: Session Routing Bugs: CLI routing to wrong session, WeChat ID inconsistency, and session deadlock from message flooding

question: Should #88204 remain as a human coordination tracker, or should maintainers split it into focused TUI, sessions_send, WeChat plugin-boundary, background-event isolation, and meaningful-activity issues with named owners?
rationale: The source-backed parts are real, but the bundled report crosses core runtime, external plugin ownership, queue/session semantics, and UI activity taxonomy, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Split And Route
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella while creating or linking focused owner-scoped issues for each unresolved subproblem, then close it only after the subissues cover the full scope.

options.title: Narrow To Core Only
options.body: Retitle the issue around the source-proven core TUI/sessions_send/updatedAt pieces and move WeChat plugin and flood-deadlock proof to separate follow-ups.

options.title: Close In Favor Of Existing Partials
options.body: Close this as overlapping #51028 and #93255, accepting that the WeChat and flood/deadlock pieces would need new reports if they recur.

recommendation.title: Split And Route
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella while creating or linking focused owner-scoped issues for each unresolved subproblem, then close it only after the subissues cover the full scope.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session UI, gateway session organization, TUI lifecycle, and WeChat docs history make this the best available owner for deciding how to split the tracker.
